Inspect a session

Source: R/session_api.R
sas_session_accessors.Rd

Functional accessors of a sas_session(): the WORK data sets (trailing blanks of character values removed, as in sas_run() results), their metadata, the macro variables and the cumulative listing of all submissions (sas_log() gives the cumulative log). sas_session_close() closes the PROC SQL connection.

Usage

sas_work(session, trim = TRUE)

sas_session_add(session, work)

sas_meta(session)

sas_macro_vars(session, scope = c("global", "automatic"))

sas_listing(session)

sas_session_close(session)

Arguments

session

A session from sas_session().

trim

TRUE (trailing blanks of character values removed) or FALSE (the values as stored, padded to the variable length).

work

Named list of data frames to add to (or replace in) WORK.

scope

"global" (user-defined global macro variables) or "automatic" (automatic macro variables such as SYSCC).

Value

sas_work(): named list of tibbles. sas_meta(): named list of variable metadata. sas_macro_vars(): named list of character values. sas_listing(): character vector. sas_session_add(), sas_session_close(): the session, invisibly.

Examples

s <- sas_session()
sas_run("%let study = X01; data a; x = 1; put x=; run;", session = s)
#> 
#> ── Log ──
#> 
#> No ERRORs or WARNINGs
#> 1          %let study = X01; data a; x = 1; put x=; run;
#> 
#> x=1
#> NOTE: The data set WORK.A has 1 observations and 1 variables.
#> ── WORK data sets ──
#> 
#> WORK.A: 1 obs, 1 vars
#> Levels: L1
names(sas_work(s))
#> [1] "a"
sas_macro_vars(s)
#> $study
#> [1] "X01"
#> 
sas_log(s)
#> 1          %let study = X01; data a; x = 1; put x=; run;
#> 
#> x=1
#> NOTE: The data set WORK.A has 1 observations and 1 variables.
sas_session_close(s)
